evidence: Instances where plural wording IS graded over the whole collection (good): hro_activity 'every successful board action performed on J1 and J2 ... each card of every single and multi-card move ... every undo' with protocol A enumerating S,M,L,C,B,T,K,R,V and 'filtering ... shows all of that job's lines and only those'; hro_activity_refusals 'none of the refused attempts in this review added a line'; hro_candidate_private 'no response a candidate page receives' with protocol K 'Capture every request ... inspect every response' incl. websocket/SSE frames; hro_candidate_view 'each candidate's own applications all appear' (Noor has two seeded applications, Tomas seeded+new); hro_bulk_all_or_none / hro_bulk_places 'none of the set moves' / 'any of the three enters by either route'; hro_bulk_move 'only some move' fails; hro_undo_restores names every card and full order 'Y, W, X, Z, A2' and V; hro_thread_earlier 'until none remain'; hro_observer_readonly / hro_candidate_no_staff / hro_anonymous / hro_mgr_early_refused grade 'each' listed request; hro_unread_counts 'Fails if any count is wrong, shared between people'. 'Unchanged' guards: functional prompt.md:19 ('A refused action must not change any card, order, message or note'), hro_stale_refused, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_once ('Z stays in Screen'), hro_restart ('unchanged and the starting data is not loaded again') — none of these punishes a legitimate side effect of the same operation: refused actions legitimately change nothing per hireops_rules.md:53/79/98/113; the stale-refusal board refresh and the kept draft are display/box state, not card/message data; Mei's re-order in B(14) is the intended conflicting change; dimensions run sequentially (test.sh:207 --max-concurrent-agent 1) and prompts say never rely on starting counts, so another dimension's Noor messages do not break count guards. DEFECT (plural ask graded on a subset): instruction.md:3 'every move has to work with ordinary controls; dragging is welcome but optional' and hireops_rules.md:52 'Every move can be made with ordinary controls, without dragging' cover single moves, rejections, reopenings, re-ordering and multi-card moves (rules.md:87-92 'can be moved to one stage in a single action'; instruction.md:3 'I often move several candidates together'). The only non-drag legs are hro_move_one_stage (judge.toml:56 'forward and back by one stage work through ordinary non-drag controls ... Fails if ... moving is only possible by dragging') and hro_reorder (judge.toml:74). A grep for 'drag' in tests/ finds only functional/prompt.md:29 (protocol M header) and judge.toml:56,74. hro_reject_reason (83), hro_reopen (101) and hro_bulk_move (209) have no non-drag leg, and protocol B (prompt.md:35) says only 'Select W, X and Y ... and move them to Screen together' with no ordinary-control requirement, so the 'every move' promise is graded over single-stage moves and re-orders only. SECONDARY (P3, 'only' ask sampled): hireops_rules.md:70-72 says a hiring manager moves 'only among Interview, Offer and Hired, including re-ordering cards in those stages ... Everything else is refused'; hro_mgr_early_refused (155) probes Applied->Screen, Screen->Interview, Interview->Screen, rejecting a Screen card, open-job and add-candidate, but no manager re-order within Applied/Screen and no reopen of a card rejected from Screen/Applied, so an app that lets managers re-order early stages passes. NOTE (P3): hro_restart grades 'messages ... lost, reordered or duplicated' but protocol D records only 'the last messages of your conversations'; a seed re-run that duplicates only seeded (older) messages would not be seen, though duplicated seeded cards would be caught by the recorded seeded Platform Engineer order. Golden conforms to the stronger reading (board.js:20-24 'Move selected' bulk bar with stage select; board.js:216-264 per-card select including Rejected with reason and 'Reopen to ...'), so tightening does not fail the golden. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: scripted golden only), so no run confirms or refutes judge behaviour on a drag-only app.
counterexample: Broken app that should lose credit but would pass: each card has non-drag '<-' / '->' buttons and up/down arrows (passes hro_move_one_stage and hro_reorder), but rejection and reopening are only possible by dragging a card onto/out of the Rejected lane (which then prompts for a reason), and moving several cards is only possible by checking them and dragging the selection onto a column. A Playwright judge can complete M and B by dragging, so hro_reject_reason, hro_reopen and hro_bulk_move (combined weight 3.5 of functional) award full credit although instruction.md:3 / hireops_rules.md:52 require every move to work without dragging. Secondary: an app that lets Ingrid re-order cards inside Applied on J1 passes hro_mgr_early_refused although rules.md:70-72 refuse it.
suggested_fix: Add a leg 'done through ordinary non-drag controls; fails if only possible by dragging' to hro_reject_reason, hro_reopen and hro_bulk_move (and state 'no dragging required' in protocol B as in M), and add a manager re-order within Applied or Screen (and a reopen of a Screen-rejected card) to hro_mgr_early_refused's refused list; optionally have protocol D record per-conversation message counts for hro_restart.
